subject: Budget range validation - Aurora Payments
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Park <sophie.park@aurorapayments.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-01T14:32:00-07:00
Subject: Budget range validation - Aurora Payments (post-call recap)

Hi Sophie — great to talk earlier. Quick recap from today's discovery and a couple of asks so we can get you a tailored quote: 

What we covered:
- Primary use: realtime fraud-review assistant and transaction enrichment for checkout flows.
- Expected query profile: short prompts (~150 tokens) on classification + longer context for batch enrichment (~1k tokens).
- Success criteria: <200ms 95th perc latency for realtime routes; 99.9% availability; predictable unit economics.

As discussed, can you confirm the following so we can validate the right pricing tier and procurement path?
1) Estimated monthly token volume (rough band is fine; e.g., 100M, 1B, 5B).
2) Target monthly spend band or budget range.
3) Any procurement thresholds (PO approval levels, required SSO/SAML, security questionnaire cadence).

Quick note on how we think about unit economics (so we have the right knobs): we price by $/1M tokens with volume tiers and optional reserved/dedicated capacity for larger commits. If you have a target $/1M token number that you'd like us to use for the quote, include that and we'll model out monthly spend across the band.

Next steps: if you can reply with the three items above, I’ll run the numbers and send a preliminary quote + procurement checklist.

Thanks — talk soon.
—
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0178
Redwood Inference

From: Sophie Park <sophie.park@aurorapayments.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-02T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Budget range validation - Aurora Payments

Hi Marissa — thanks for the recap, really helpful. Answers below: 

1) Estimated monthly token volume: we expect between ~500M and 2B tokens/month in steady-state (peak testing months could be higher).
2) Target monthly budget band: approximately $5k to $25k/month initially (we're modeling low and high-growth scenarios).
3) Procurement thresholds: any order > $15k requires Finance review; > $25k needs VP-level approval and a standard security/compliance packet. We also require a PO to process payments.

We run a quarterly security review; if Redwood can share SOC2 and basic architecture notes now, that speeds legal. I’m looping in our procurement contact, Carlos Rivera (carlos.rivera@aurorapayments.com), in case you need to coordinate PO/terms. I’ll also attach our procurement thresholds doc.

Appreciate you modeling the unit economics — our target $/1M tokens goal is roughly $10/1M (we're trying to benchmark against other vendors).

Best,
Sophie Park
Head of Product, Aurora Payments
sophie.park@aurorapayments.com

Attachment: aurora_procurement_thresholds.pdf

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-10-03T11:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Budget range validation - Aurora Payments

Thanks Sophie — this is perfect and very actionable. Based on the band and your $10/1M target, I ran a quick model and included a couple of committed-pricing scenarios so procurement has a clear ask. Summary below (rounded):

Assumptions:
- Volume band: 500M — 2B tokens/month
- Prospect target: $10 / 1M tokens

Committed-tier pricing model (example tiers we can propose):
- 500M/month: committed price ~ $9 / 1M => monthly spend ≈ $4,500
- 2B/month: committed price ~ $7 / 1M => monthly spend ≈ $14,000

Takeaways:
- Both committed tiers sit inside your target budget band ($5k–$25k) and below the VP approval threshold at the upper committed price.
- If you prefer a month-to-month usage plan (no commit), list price would be higher; committed 3–12 month terms yield the unit economics above.
- For customers at the 2B/month scale, we also offer Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity) which can push to mid-high single-digit $/1M and provide tighter latency SLOs.

Next suggested steps:
1) I’ll attach a preliminary quote for the 3-month committed trial at the 500M and 2B tiers so you can see line items (attached: preliminary_quote_aurora.pdf).
2) If that looks good, Carlos — could you confirm the PO process and whether a three-month pilot PO is acceptable?
3) We’ll also send SOC2 + short architecture note to speed legal (Dylan, can you add the SOC2 link and SI architecture stub to the quote packet?).

If you want, I can put together two quick options in writing (3-month pilot and 12-month committed) and we can hand that to procurement with a recommended lane. Happy to jump on a quick call with Carlos and your procurement team if helpful.

Best,
Marissa

Attachment: preliminary_quote_aurora.pdf

Ask (Dylan / Rishi):

Goal: turn around formal quote + docs and send to Carlos by EOD 2026-10-06. I’ll draft the cover email and send once you confirm numbers.
